Zero values, arrays, maps and strings.

=== every type has a zero value
-- script/main --
class Box {}
class Zeroes {
  n: number
  s: string
  b: bool
  box: Box
  xs: number[]
  m: Map<string, number>
}
export function main(): string {
  const z = new Zeroes()
  let local: number
  return str(z.n) + "|" + z.s + "|" + str(z.b) + "|" + str(z.box == null) + "|" + str(z.xs == null) + "|" + str(z.m == null) + "|" + str(local)
}
-- want --
"0||false|true|true|true|0"

=== a null array or map reads as empty
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  let xs: number[]
  let m: Map<string, number>
  let n = 0
  for (const x of xs) { n += 100 }
  return n + xs.length + m.size + m.get("missing") + xs.indexOf(1) + (m.has("a") ? 10 : 0)
}
-- want --
-1

=== writing to a null array fails
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  let xs: number[]
  xs.push(1)
  return 1
}
-- eval error --
script/main:3:6: push on a null number[]

=== a missing key gives the zero value
-- script/main --
export function main(): string {
  const m = new Map<string, string>()
  return "[" + m.get("nope") + "]"
}
-- want --
"[]"

=== null goes into any reference
-- script/main --
class A {}
export function main(): bool {
  let a: A = null
  let xs: number[] = null
  return a == null && xs == null
}
-- want --
true

=== null alone has no type
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  let a = null
  return 1
}
-- compile error --
give a a type

=== an empty array needs its type
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  let a = []
  return 1
}
-- compile error --
give the array a type

=== primitives are never null
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  let n: number = null
  return n
}
-- compile error --
n is a null, not a number

=== arrays
-- script/main --
export function main(): number[] {
  let xs: number[] = []
  xs.push(3, 1, 4)
  xs[1] = 9
  xs.push(xs.pop() + 1)
  return xs.slice(1).slice(-2)
}
-- want --
[9, 5]

=== array searches and joins
-- script/main --
export function main(): string {
  const xs = ["a", "b", "c"]
  return str(xs.indexOf("c")) + str(xs.includes("z")) + xs.join("-")
}
-- want --
"2falsea-b-c"

=== an index out of range fails
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  const xs = [1, 2]
  return xs[2]
}
-- eval error --
index 2 is out of range (length 2)

=== a fractional index fails
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  const xs = [1, 2]
  return xs[0.5]
}
-- eval error --
index 0.5 is out of range

=== arrays of arrays
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  const grid: number[][] = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
  grid[1][0] = 7
  return grid[1][0] + grid[0].length
}
-- want --
9

=== arrays hold one type
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  const xs = [1, "a"]
  return 1
}
-- compile error --
an array of number can't hold a string

=== maps keep their order
-- script/main --
export function main(): Map<string, number> {
  const m = new Map<string, number>()
  m.set("b", 1)
  m.set("a", 2)
  m.set("c", 3)
  m.set("b", 4)
  m.delete("a")
  return m
}
-- want --
{"b": 4, "c": 3}

=== map keys and values
-- script/main --
export function main(): string {
  const m = new Map<number, string>()
  m.set(2, "two")
  m.set(1, "one")
  return m.keys().join(",") + " " + m.values().join(",") + " " + str(m.size) + str(m.has(2))
}
-- want --
"2,1 two,one 2true"

=== maps are read with get
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  const m = new Map<string, number>()
  return m["a"]
}
-- compile error --
read a map with get(key)

=== map keys are numbers or strings
-- script/main --
class A {}
export function main(): number {
  const m = new Map<A, number>()
  return 1
}
-- compile error --
a map's keys are numbers or strings

=== strings
-- script/main --
export function main(): string[] {
  const s = "  Héllo World  ".trim()
  return [s.toUpperCase(), s.toLowerCase(), s.slice(1, 4), str(s.length), str(s.indexOf("W")), str(s.startsWith("Hé")), str(s.endsWith("x")), str(s.includes("lo"))]
}
-- want --
["HÉLLO WORLD", "héllo world", "éll", "11", "6", "true", "false", "true"]

=== split
-- script/main --
export function main(): string[] { return "a,b,,c".split(",") }
-- want --
["a", "b", "", "c"]

=== arrays have a length but no other field
-- script/main --
export function main(): number { return [1].size }
-- compile error --
a number[] has no field size

=== arrays stop at the limit
-- script/main --
export function main(): number {
  const xs: number[] = []
  while (true) { xs.push(1) }
  return 1
}
-- eval error --
an array longer than 10000

=== the conditional's sides agree
-- script/main --
class A {}
export function main(): bool {
  const a: A = true ? null : new A()
  return a == null
}
-- want --
true

=== an element is set in the array as the value left it
-- script/main --
class Box {
  xs: number[] = [0]
  grow(): number {
    this.xs.push(1)
    return 7
  }
  shrink(): number {
    this.xs.pop()
    return 9
  }
}
export function main(): number[] {
  const b = new Box()
  b.xs[0] = b.grow()
  return b.xs
}
-- want --
[7, 1]

=== an element the value removed can't be set
-- script/main --
class Box {
  xs: number[] = [0, 0]
  shrink(): number {
    this.xs.pop()
    return 9
  }
}
export function main(): number {
  const b = new Box()
  b.xs[1] = b.shrink()
  return 1
}
-- eval error --
index 1 is out of range (length 1)
